summary: Compete for Mars is a online multiplayer game (up to 4 players) set in a Martian base, built as a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Kids compete in a series of mini-games, such as driving a rover across real Martian terrain, repairing an electrical circuit, suiting up for an EVA or surviving a solar storm, to find out who survives and makes it back to Earth. Along the way, players must manage limited resources and deal with sabotage and deception from rivals. Each mini-game is built around real NASA science and mission data, so children learn how life-support systems, space weather, radiation and spacesuits actually work while they play. Our goal is to make space operations approachable and exciting for young audiences and to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers.
details:
Compete for Mars is a browser-based multiplayer survival game that introduces players to the challenges of maintaining a Martian outpost through strategy, competition, and interactive engineering tasks.

The story begins at Valkyrie Station on Mars, where a powerful solar storm causes critical damage. An emergency protocol reveals that the remaining life support and fuel can sustain only one passenger. Introduced through an illustrated comic, this fictional scenario gives players a clear objective: manage their supplies, overcome mission challenges, and become the last surviving astronaut.

Up to four players join a room using a code and choose a profession: Engineer, Pilot, Biologist, or Medic. Each profession offers a different balance of food and energy capacity. Players must manage food, energy, health, and accumulated radiation throughout the match.

From the second round onward, players secretly choose action cards before tackling the next mission. These decisions include sharing limited supplies, resting, undertaking risky expeditions, activating radiation protection, or sabotaging rivals. Choices interact: when several astronauts select the same supply card, they divide the available resources.

The game features seven playable minigames, each connected to a different aspect of space exploration:
- Water Pipeline: reconnect pipes supporting the habitat’s water recovery and hydroponic systems.
- NASA Survival Trivia: answer questions about life support, radiation, power, space farming, and exploration, with educational explanations and source notes.
- Mars Rover Traverse: navigate a 3D Martian landscape, balancing travel time, terrain difficulty, and battery consumption.
- Suit-Up Sequence: complete timing and sequence challenges to prepare a spacesuit for an emergency EVA.
- Signal Modulation: adjust a communication signal and filter interference in a scenario inspired by NASA’s Deep Space Network.
- Solar Storm Deflector: protect the base in an arcade challenge featuring predefined solar-event scenarios referencing NASA’s DONKI database.
- Anomaly Detection: compare circuit diagrams and identify faulty components before a habitat blackout.
Our central creative idea is that resource management changes how the next minigame feels. Hunger and fatigue affect actions, timing, or scoring, depending on the challenge. Supplies therefore have immediate consequences beyond a number on a dashboard. Radiation persists across rounds, creating another reason to balance short-term rewards against future risks.

The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about STEM and help players understand the connections between astronaut wellbeing, infrastructure, and mission success. The experience uses simplified, fictional mechanics to make these trade-offs approachable and entertaining.

We developed the project using TypeScript, React, Vite, Node.js, Express, and Socket.IO, with WebGL, Canvas, and SVG for graphics. GitHub supported collaboration, and the prototype runs on a Google Cloud virtual machine with Nginx and HTTPS. AI coding assistants supported development, while our team directed game design, visual assets, content, integration, and testing.

Our design priorities included clear mission briefings, varied controls, replayability, fair starting scenarios, browser access without installation, and a modular architecture that allows additional minigames to be developed independently.

Play the prototype: https://34.175.2.182/
